title: Remove Duplicate Numbers
statement: Given an integer array nums, return a new array containing only the first occurrence of each number in original order.
think: What is the task asking? Keep only the first appearance of each number.
What is the key operation? Know whether a number was already seen.
What wording signals stand out? Remove duplicates, unique values, first occurrence.
Which pattern fits? HashSet, together with a result list.
What is the brute force idea? For each number, scan the result built so far.
What is the better/optimal idea? Track seen numbers in a HashSet and append unseen values to result.
What are the edge cases? Already unique input, all duplicates, negative values.
What is the complexity? O(n) time and O(n) space.
How would I explain it in an interview? I keep a set of seen values and a list for the output order.
algorithm: Create HashSet<int> seen and List<int> result
If seen.Add(num) succeeds -> append num to result
interview: I would use a HashSet to track which numbers were already seen and a result list to preserve original order.
ru: Set отвечает на вопрос 'видели ли мы уже это число', а список хранит ответ в исходном порядке.
visualExplanation:
nums = [1,2,2,3,1,4]
1 -> add to set and result
2 -> add
2 -> skip
3 -> add
1 -> skip
4 -> add

critical: Use only HashSet and lose original order in explanation
important: Forget to keep first occurrence only
nice: Do not mention why result list is needed

gaps: Important: combine HashSet with output list
Nice to have: explain order preservation
whyThisPattern: This is mainly a HashSet problem because seen/not-seen is the core logic, with a list used to preserve order.
whyNotOtherPatterns: Not Dictionary, because counts are unnecessary.
Not Sorting, because sorting would destroy original order.
